headline: Major M7.7 Earthquake Strikes Indonesia's Flores Region as Hurricane Lala Batters Entire Hawaiian Island Chain
overview: A powerful M7.7 earthquake struck off the north coast of Flores, Indonesia late on August 14 UTC, triggering initial tsunami warnings and a USGS orange alert for a region with a history of deadly seismic events. Simultaneously, Hurricane Lala — now bearing down on the entire Hawaiian island chain from the Big Island to Oahu and Kauai — represents a historic and potentially catastrophic landfalling storm. A multi-day extreme heat emergency continues across the central and southern United States, Indiana's White River has shattered its 1913 flood record, and the Colombia M7.4 earthquake rescue effort remains critical.

events.title: M7.7 Earthquake Strikes Flores Region, Indonesia — USGS Orange Alert
events.location: 68 km NNW of Ende, Flores, Indonesia
events.summary: A major magnitude 7.7 earthquake struck the Flores region of Indonesia at 21:58 UTC on August 14, at a very shallow depth of just 10 km, triggering initial tsunami assessment and a USGS orange alert level. The shallow depth and location near Flores — one of the most seismically hazardous arcs in the world — raises significant concern for casualties and structural damage; 37 felt reports were logged rapidly. The Flores region suffered a devastating M7.8 earthquake in 1992 that killed over 2,500 people, making this event closely watched by emergency authorities.

events.title: Hurricane Lala Makes Historic Strike on Hawaiʻi — Entire Island Chain Under Warnings
events.location: Hawaiʻi Island, Maui, Oahu, Kauai, Hawaiʻi, USA
events.summary: Hurricane Lala has significantly escalated beyond yesterday's forecast track, now subjecting the entire Hawaiian island chain to hurricane and tropical storm conditions simultaneously — a historically rare event. The Big Island's southeast coast faces Category 1-equivalent winds of 74–110 mph, while Tropical Storm Warnings now extend to Oahu (including Honolulu) and all of Kauai, and a Flood Watch covers the entire state through Sunday night. The storm's potential to make a direct hurricane landfall on the Big Island would be the first such event in recorded Hawaiian history, with catastrophic flash flooding, dangerous surf, and sustained hurricane-force winds threatening communities across multiple islands.

events.title: Indiana White River Shatters 1913 Flood Record — Governor Declares Emergency
events.summary: Indiana's catastrophic flooding has escalated dramatically, with the White River near Indianapolis breaking its all-time gauge record set during the Great Flood of 1913 — a significant threshold not breached in over a century. The governor has declared a state of emergency as major to record flooding propagates downstream along the White River from Muncie to Edwardsport, with NWS Flood Warnings active through as late as August 24 for some counties. Dozens of river gauges remain at major or record flood stage across central Indiana, and the Wabash River system is also rising, with the disaster expected to take weeks to fully recede.

events.title: Colombia M7.4 Earthquake — Rescue Ongoing, Death Toll Continues to Rise
events.location: San José del Palmar, Chocó Department, Colombia
events.summary: The M7.4 earthquake that struck near San José del Palmar on August 10 maintains a USGS red alert — the highest level — with 1,151 felt reports logged and the death toll surpassing 250 as of August 14. Rescue operations continue to be hampered by terrain, aftershocks, and damaged infrastructure in the remote Chocó department, one of Colombia's most isolated regions. The earthquake remains one of the deadliest seismic events in Colombian history, and international aid teams are still actively engaged in search and recovery operations.

events.title: Multi-State Extreme Heat Emergency Expands — Heat Index Hits 115°F Across South and Midwest
events.location: Arkansas, Missouri, Kansas, Tennessee, Mississippi, Louisiana, Georgia, South Carolina, USA
events.summary: Extreme Heat Warnings blanketed a vast swath of the central and southern United States on August 15, with heat index values reaching 115°F in coastal Georgia and South Carolina, and 113–114°F across Arkansas and Louisiana. The heat dome has now expanded eastward to include middle Tennessee (up to 112°F heat index in Nashville) and is forecast to persist through at least Sunday evening, with an Extreme Heat Watch already posted for the Phoenix metropolitan area through next Friday with temperatures of 109–113°F. The Climate Prediction Center warns that a greater-than-60% chance of extreme heat persists across the region through August 21, raising serious public health concerns.

events.title: Timber Fire Threatens Big Sur Landmarks — Nearly 4,000 Acres Burned
events.summary: The Timber Fire in California's iconic Big Sur coastal range has grown to nearly 4,000 acres, threatening tourist destinations and prompting evacuations and closures of portions of the area as of August 12–15. Firefighters are battling steep terrain, dry fuels, and erratic winds in one of California's most ecologically sensitive and visited landscapes. Red Flag Warnings remain active across parts of the Pacific Northwest, reflecting heightened wildfire risk across the broader Western US amid an active monsoon pattern delivering dry lightning.

events.title: Europe's Fifth Heatwave of 2026 Persists — Berlin 34.8°C, Paris 33.5°C, Drought Deepens
events.summary: Western Europe's fifth heatwave of 2026 continues on August 15, with Berlin reaching 34.8°C and Paris 33.5°C — slightly cooler than yesterday's 38.4°C Paris peak but still well above seasonal norms with no meaningful rainfall across the region. The prolonged heat is deepening an already severe drought across France, Germany, and the UK, where London recorded 27.4°C with zero precipitation, stressing agricultural systems and river levels. The extended duration of this heatwave sequence — five distinct events since June — is being attributed to persistent high-pressure blocking patterns consistent with long-term climate trends.
